svg.text: Template rendering matrix — every Copier answer renders
Scenario: the default render is canonical, and each answer changes exactly what it promises
What the default project looks like
Each answer changes exactly what it promises

g.text: Given a project is rendered from the working-branch template with every
default Copier answer
Off-camera: the working-branch template copier-copied with every default answer — the
reference render every other card in this journey is measured against.
Then the rendered tree delivers the canonical docker, compose and
project layout
The default render: docker-ce and compose are present, podman and ansible are absent,
project/ is delivered. Twinned with filesystem checks.
And the root Taskfile wires in the default docker-ce and compose
toolchain
The generated root Taskfile includes the docker-ce and project taskfiles, never podman —
proven by grepping its own content.
And the CI pipeline ships the default docker-in-docker variables and
release gate
The rendered CI variables target the shared docker-in-docker host, and the release job
carries its after-script security gate.
And the project's own governance and language config are delivered
The project's own answers file, Gherkin language rule and renovate fast-forward automerge
rule are all in place.
Given the default answers render docker-ce, compose and English as the
baseline
Off-camera: a fresh default render — docker-ce and compose present, Gherkin in English — the
baseline every answer below changes exactly one part of.
Then choosing podman as the runtime replaces docker-ce and compose with
podman config
container_runtime=podman: the podman Taskfile appears, docker-ce and the compose file are
both gone, and the root Taskfile points at podman instead.
And turning off docker compose drops the compose file but keeps
docker-ce
use_docker_compose=false: the compose file disappears while the docker-ce taskfile stays
exactly as in the default render.
And turning on Ansible delivers its config and lint tooling
ansible_enabled=true: .config/ansible and .config/ansible-lint both appear, and the root
Taskfile picks up the new include.
And choosing a self-hosted CI platform changes the docker-in-docker
variables
ci_platform=gitlab_self_hosted with an empty host/certdir: the shared DOCKER_HOST is gone
and DOCKER_TLS_CERTDIR renders empty.
And turning off project mode removes the project directory entirely
project_enabled=false: the whole project/ tree is gone and the root Taskfile drops its
include.
And turning off automerge removes the fast-forward rule from the
renovate config
devsecops_automerge=false: the toolbox package rule keeps its match but drops every
automerge property, and the config stays valid JSON.
And choosing French Gherkin changes the language rule for generated
tests
gherkin_language=fr: the tests-structure rule now instructs the project to write its Gherkin
in French.
